title: ILT OS filter cannot distinguish Server 2016 from Server 2025: the collision Studio must surface

provenance.note: The emission side is native-observed: the anchored capture shows what WS2025 GPMC writes for a server OS filter (WINTHRESHOLDSRV). The CSE evaluation side (which builds the token matches) is spec-informed: all of Server 2016/2019/2022/2025 report major version 10.0, and FilterOs exposes no build-number field. Endpoint confirmation is recorded as an open question rather than silently assumed.

anchors.note: Genuine WS2025 GPMC-authored drive item carrying twelve FilterOs predicates.

predicate.operator_goal: Target only recent Windows Server builds (operator believes Server 2016 and Server 2025 can be told apart)

match_semantics.token_meaning: Windows 10/Server Threshold server family: matches every server reporting major.minor 10.0, which is all of Server 2016, 2019, 2022, and 2025
derivations: FilterOs has no build-number attribute; class/version/type/edition/sp are the entire match surface (Studio's ilt.py models the same five).

Because the whole server family shares 10.0, no FilterOs predicate can separate Server 2016 from Server 2025; the only server tokens GPMC emits are the family tokens (WINTHRESHOLDSRV for the whole 10.0 family) plus type/edition refinements.
Emission is native-observed (anchor); CSE evaluation per build is spec-informed until an endpoint run confirms; the operator-surfacing requirement below holds under either outcome.

studio_must_surface.trigger: An operator authors or edits an ILT os predicate targeting the server 10.x family
studio_must_surface.message_substance: This filter matches all of Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022, and 2025 and cannot distinguish them; build-level targeting requires a different predicate class (for example a WMI query on Win32_OperatingSystem BuildNumber)
studio_must_surface.boundary: The limitation is honest at authoring time, import time, and in any exported review artifact; it is not buried in documentation

open_questions: Endpoint confirmation on the qualified client and a Server 2016/2025 pair: does a WINTHRESHOLDSRV filter match exactly the builds listed, with no surprise exclusions?
